claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: ledger now uses the round-1 text. volumes.md: CSI/FlexVolume "allow volume plugins to be developed independently of the Kubernetes code base, and deployed (installed) on Kubernetes clusters as extensions." Note: "CSI drivers may not be compatible across all Kubernetes releases. Please check the specific CSI driver's documentation for supported deployments steps for each Kubernetes release and a compatibility matrix." Section 4 now states the release condition.

Round 2: ledger now hedged ('usually'; node part 'on each node where Pods may use its volumes'). Docs name a "CSI controller plugin" and a "CSI node plugin"; "containerized CSI node plugins are typically deployed as privileged containers." Sections 3, 4 and summary line 2 now carry 'usually'.

Round 2: covers the new section-4 sentence on waiting for the first Pod. storage-classes.md: WaitForFirstConsumer "will delay the binding and provisioning of a PersistentVolume until a Pod using the PersistentVolumeClaim is created"; "The following plugins support WaitForFirstConsumer with dynamic provisioning: CSI volumes, provided that the specific CSI driver supports this". Provisioner and Delete passages as in round 1.

Round 2: ledger and section 4 now say the node part mounts the volume; attach is no longer assigned to it. Consistent with CSIDriver.attachRequired (attach via the attach-detach controller and external-attacher, ControllerPublishVolume) and volumes.md csi fields NodeStageVolume/NodePublishVolume.

Storage Classes > Provisioner: "You are not restricted to specifying the "internal" provisioners listed here ... You can also run and specify external provisioners, which are independent programs ... Authors of external provisioners have full discretion over ... what volume plugin it uses (including Flex)". So provisioner may name a non-CSI provisioner. Volumes > csi: driver must correspond to GetPluginInfoResponse name.

Capture outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/csi.txt: "standard   rancher.io/local-path", one Pod "local-path-provisioner-...-...   donhang-control-plane", csidrivers "No resources found". storage-class.txt: "standard (default)", PV folder /var/local-path-provisioner/... README: "the Local Path Provisioner will create either hostPath or local based persistent volume on the node automatically" (hostPath/local PV types, not csi); README never mentions CSI.

Round 2: ledger now hedged ('usually describes itself'). csi-driver-v1.md: "CSIDriver captures information about a Container Storage Interface (CSI) volume driver deployed on the cluster"; "metadata.Name indicates the name of the CSI driver that this object refers to; it MUST be the same name returned by the CSI GetPluginName() call"; "CSIDriver objects are non-namespaced." csi.txt: "No resources found".

Round 3: ledger now 'extra snapshot pieces (CRDs and a snapshot controller) installed in the cluster alongside Kubernetes'; section 4 says 'the cluster has the extra snapshot pieces installed alongside Kubernetes'. volume-snapshots.md L51: "VolumeSnapshot support is only available for CSI drivers." L66: "The CRDs and snapshot controller installations are the responsibility of the Kubernetes distribution." Condition kept; who installs is left open, which the docs support. dataSource provisioning as in round 2.

Round 2: ledger now 'With many drivers' and drops 'or the cluster'; sections 3, 4, 6, summary 5 and quiz q3/q5 follow. Volume Snapshots: "a VolumeSnapshot represents a snapshot of a volume on a storage system" (location left to the driver). Longhorn 1.9: "Snapshots are stored locally, as a part of each replica of a volume" - an instance of the hedged case.

Storage Classes: "When a PVC does not specify a storageClassName, the default StorageClass is used." Capture storage-class.txt: "standard (default)   rancher.io/local-path". Repo db.yaml volumeClaimTemplates has no storageClassName (comment: "With no storageClassName it gets the cluster's default StorageClass.").

Repo: base/db.yaml StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates "data" with no storageClassName (gets default standard). scripts/k8s/db-backup.sh L63-65: "mkdir -p backups/staging" and kubectl cp ... "backups/staging/$file"; capture db-backup.txt: "== the newest dumps, copied to backups/staging/".

scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh: "kubectl() { command kubectl --context kind-donhang \"$@\"; }" and "show() { echo \"\$ $*\"; \"$@\"; }"; lessons_cluster comment "one control-plane node, two workers". deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml: one control-plane + two worker roles. csi.sh L18-20 (lesson excerpt): echo "\$ kubectl get csidrivers" then kubectl get csidrivers 2>&1; capture shows the message in the output.

Repo deploy/k8s/bare-metal/longhorn-storageclass.yaml: "# Longhorn's CSI driver, installed with Longhorn itself." / "provisioner: driver.longhorn.io". Longhorn 1.9 Concepts: "Longhorn is managed in Kubernetes via a CSI Plugin." "The required Kubernetes CSI Driver images will be deployed automatically by the longhorn driver deployer." Storage class parameters: "For Longhorn, that is always \"driver.longhorn.io\"."

Round 2: ledger and section 6 carry the release condition and say only that Kubernetes code is not changed. volumes.md: plugins "deployed (installed) on Kubernetes clusters as extensions"; "CSI drivers may not be compatible across all Kubernetes releases." Zero issues in round 3 (targeted): re-read section 4 snapshot sentence and claim 8 against refs volume-snapshots.md; quiz unchanged since round 2.
